title: fix(runtime)!: an active ADR-0069 gate that cannot read the session answers 503 at the dispatcher's seam
body:
Fixes #23245
Clause-②: no (narrowing: an active gate's outage now refuses what it served)

## What this changes

`HttpDispatcher.enforceAuthGate` (`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`) read the session with `.catch(() => undefined)` and wrapped the whole decision in `catch { return null }`. So while the auth service could not answer, an active ADR-0069 gate took the failed read for "no session" and admitted, on every route the runtime dispatcher serves. REST's `computeExecCtx` answers the same window `503` under #13906's decision 2 (option B, "an *active* auth gate whose session re-read fails answers **503**"), and so does the dispatcher plugin's declared-endpoint fallback since #23190.

Now, once `isAuthGateActive()` has answered `true`, a failure to read the session throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('auth_gate', err)`. The outer net re-raises that brand alone (`rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable`, the shape core prescribes) and keeps failing open on every other fault. The call sits above `dispatch()`'s own `try`, so the error leaves `dispatch()`, and the transport's existing error exit (`errorResponseBase` in `dispatcher-plugin.ts`) answers it `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. That is the exit the identity step's and the membership gate's outages already take. No second rendering is added.

## The arms, case for case

| gate state | dispatcher before | dispatcher after | REST `computeExecCtx` | declared-endpoint fallback |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| no gate feature active (no read is made) | admitted | admitted, unchanged | admitted | admitted |
| `isAuthGateActive()` throws | admitted | admitted, unchanged | admitted | admitted |
| active, the session read rejects | **admitted** | **503** | 503 | 503 |
| active, the session API cannot be obtained, or the header bag cannot be normalised | admitted | **503** | anonymous (see note) | 503 |
| active, the read resolves with no posture (no session, an un-held user) | admitted | admitted, unchanged | admitted | admitted |
| active, the read carries a posture | 403 with the gate code | 403, unchanged | 403 | 403 |

Note on the fourth row. On REST those steps run in the identity half of `computeExecCtx`, before its gate block, and a fault there falls to the method's outer net, so the caller becomes anonymous. The dispatcher's gate runs after identity has been decided, so "anonymous" is not an answer this seam can give: the choice is to admit or to refuse. This PR refuses, as the in-package sibling `readGatedSessionUser` does for exactly these steps. An active gate whose session read could not even be made has failed to read, in the ruling's terms. The arm is named here so the review can rule on it.

## Pin

`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.auth-gate-outage.pin.test.ts` drives the three cases through `dispatch()`:

1. **Outage:** an active gate whose session read rejects. `dispatch()` rejects with the branded error (`code` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `status` 503, `object` `auth_gate`), and the route's handler never runs.
2. **Gate off:** the same failing backend with no gate feature active is served as before. The gate makes no read of its own, measured as a read count (an active gate on the same request reads exactly once more than an inactive one).
3. **Active and clear:** a read that resolves with an un-held user, or with no session, is admitted.

A positive control rides beside them: an expired password on a route the allow-list does not name gets the gate's 403, so a green "served" cannot mean that the gate never ran. A second block mounts the real dispatcher plugin on a recording server and reads the wire, one row per gate state: the outage is answered `503` with an envelope that parses under `BaseResponseSchema` and `ApiErrorSchema` and carries `code: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; gate off keeps its `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`; active and clear keeps the route's own `501`; held keeps `403 PASSWORD_EXPIRED`.

**Negative control** (one shot, not kept as a test). With the fix committed (`ebf5848f6`), `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the outer net with `catch { return null }` (anchor 1 hit, x1 to x0, blob `5b42c4c85e3b` to `db96181d7c71`) and ran the pin:

```text
 × CASE 1 — OUTAGE: … → `dispatch()` RESOLVED — the active gate failed open on the outage: expected undefined to be defined
 × OUTAGE on the wire: … → expected 401 to be 503 // Object.is equality
      Tests  2 failed | 7 passed (9)
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (5b42c4c85e3b) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Both outage cases went red and every control stayed green, which was the direction predicted before the run. The wire reading also confirms the "before" column: the outage used to answer `401` there, byte for byte the gate-off answer.

## Full-repo pin sweep

No pin in the repository asserts the old fail-open at this seam, so nothing needed flipping.

- Every test that wires `isAuthGateActive` (13 files) was checked. The only ones that drive a failing read on an active gate pin other seams (REST, the declared-endpoint fallback, the storage routes), and each already expects 503.
- The error code and object (`'auth_gate'`) appear only at those seams.
- The fail-open wording (`fail-open`, `fails open`, `never break dispatch`) in `packages/runtime/src` tests appears in prose only, never in an assertion on this seam.
- The full `@objectstack/runtime` suite stays green with the fix.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.root-auth-gate.test.ts` (header near line 44, and the comment near line 110) says `enforceAuthGate` fails open on "any thrown error". After this PR that is no longer true for an active gate's failed session read. The prose is not an assertion, and the file is outside this PR's claimed surface. Carrier: the next PR that touches that file.
- #23335 (in flight): its branch head `c12ba7bd0` changes only comments in `packages/core/src/security/auth-gate.ts`. The pin's posture is an expired password on a route the allow-list does not name, which that change does not touch.
- PR #23346 has merged. The 503's rendering does not go through `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts`, which is a gate's declaration file and is not imported at runtime, so the two changes are not coupled. The pin stays green on top of it.
